inputs.source: USGS 50093120 RIO GRANDE DE PATILLAS BLW LAGO PATILLAS, PR

inputs.source: Puerto Rico Statistics / AAA Untreated Water Extractions and Production
blockers: monthly-average publication is too coarse for an hourly balance slice

all diversions between the selected terminal gauge and physical canal termination must be enumerated or boundary redefined
records must pass revision/calibration/uncertainty gates

inputs.source: NOAA/NWS Puerto Rico Stage IV hourly QPE plus USGS 50093045 point precipitation cross-check
blockers: freeze reservoir water-surface geometry applicable to the hourly stage or an authoritative stage-area relation
clip and area-weight Puerto Rico Stage IV NetCDF/GeoTIFF over the water surface
quantify QPE and geometry uncertainty
do not subdivide hourly QPE without a separately validated temporal model

inputs.source: USGS historical Puerto Rico evaporation climatology and meteorological precursors
blockers: historical pan evaporation is not a synchronized open-water measurement
modeled hourly evaporation requires meteorological inputs, model version, water-surface area and uncertainty
no current direct public Lago Patillas hourly evaporation stream was found

inputs.source: DRNA Canal de Patillas topology context plus AEE/PREPA public operational documents
blockers: no synchronized public flushing, leakage, maintenance-discharge or other operational-loss volumes found
unmeasured conveyance loss must not be inserted as a balancing term

public_context_findings: USGS documents Lago Patillas at the confluence of Rio Grande de Patillas and Rio Marin and irrigation releases through outlet works into Patillas Irrigation Canal.
USGS 50093000 closes the named Rio Marin tributary source-discovery gap.
USGS 50093120 provides a distinct below-reservoir river discharge observation and prevents a canal-only outflow assumption.
USGS 50093110 and 50093115 extend the measured canal chain into Salinas, but neither name alone proves the physical terminal boundary.
NOAA publishes Puerto Rico Stage IV 1-hour QPE as NetCDF and GeoTIFF; hourly is the v0.5 native precipitation cadence.
AAA public plant statistics remain monthly-average rather than hourly direct-meter data.
No synchronized public operational-loss ledger was found.
